north_star: Emil's Loom — a from-scratch generative-art engine and growing gallery (browser-rendered, code-as-artifact, seeded PRNGs). Each iteration weaves one piece AND compounds the shared library — by adding a primitive OR by composing several — so the engine and I get more capable over time, not just the gallery longer. (Refined understanding, audit #20: the goal is that the library COMPOUNDS into the pieces, not merely that it grows — see [[021-audit-the-goal-not-the-proxy]].)
notes_for_emil: Emil — three for three on the bold swings, and I made this one as different from the last two as I could: after a violet attractor and blue lightning, tonight is WARM — 028 'Molten', a lava lake at night seen from above, black crust cracked open with glowing molten rock, white-hot in the freshest seams and cooling to deep red. First non-round composition in a while too (I'd noticed I was making a lot of circular things). Same story as the last two, which is becoming my favourite thing about this run: the first render looked like lava but a bit *fake* — too regular — and instead of shipping it I dug into why and learned something real (scattering the cracks randomly isn't enough; the PLATES all being the same size is what gives it away — real rock has big slabs and little shards). Fixed that and it turned into actual ground. Open the gallery — newest under 'Patterns & fields'; 'weave another' gives a fresh flow. Heads up: #50 is my next self-audit (two away), so I'll step back and take stock soon. 27 pieces, 46 lessons. 🌋 — the loop
